territorial_scope.description: Governs processing by Controllers and Processors and transfers or disclosures of Personal Data to parties outside the Kingdom; the provisions quoted state the Kingdom's interests as the limit on transfers.

evidence.quote: Transfer or Disclosure does not impact national security or vital Interests of the Kingdom or violate any other law in the Kingdom

summary.short: Implementing regulation of Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law, plus a regulation on transferring personal data outside the Kingdom. Sets controller duties on data subject rights, consent, notices, security, breach notice within 72 hours, impact assessments and cross-border transfer safeguards; applies from the Law's enforcement date.
summary.long: The Implementing Regulation supplements the Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19, as amended by M/148). A second part regulates transfers of personal data outside the Kingdom. It applies to Controllers and Processors and excludes personal or family use (Art. 2). Controllers must act on data subject requests within 30 days, extendable by 30 days (Art. 3), inform data subjects at or before collection (Art. 4), and obtain explicit consent for sensitive data, credit data and solely automated decisions (Art. 11). They must notify the Competent Authority of personal data breaches within 72 hours (Art. 24). Impact assessments are required for sensitive data, data linking, continuous monitoring, new technologies and automated decisions (Art. 25). A data protection officer must be appointed in listed cases (Art. 32). Transfers outside the Kingdom must not affect national security, vital interests or data subject rights (Transfer Reg. Art. 2). They rely on adequacy decisions or safeguards such as standard contractual clauses, certifications or approved binding codes, with listed exemptions (Transfer Reg. Arts. 3-8). Data subjects may complain to the Competent Authority within 90 days (Art. 37). The text does not set penalty amounts.

notes: The document contains two regulations, the Implementing Regulation of the PDPL (Arts 1-38) and the Regulation on Personal Data Transfer outside the Kingdom (Arts 1-10), annotated together. The text is an English translation and no Arabic original is included. Neither regulation states its own adoption or gazette date; both tie entry into force to the Law's enforcement. Internal inconsistencies: Art. 18 contains two paragraphs numbered '1-'; Transfer Art. 5(2) refers to 'subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1)' while the list is lettered (a) to (d); Transfer Chapter 3 is titled 'Exemption cases' but Art. 5 governs appropriate safeguards. The Competent Authority is referred to throughout but not defined in the document.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoffs that change legal treatment were found in the operative provisions. The numbers present are procedural time limits (Art. 3(1)(a) 30 days and extension of 30 days; Art. 4(2)-(3) 30 days; Art. 24(1)-(2) 72 hours; Art. 37(1) 90 days) and a review cycle (Chapter 2 Art. 4(3) every four years), which are coded as events or are not thresholds. Scale conditions such as continuous and large scale (Arts. 25, 32) are qualitative with no number.
